document.title: Housekeeping Information Translation
document.headline: Enter the facts once and generate every required representation from the same structured record

primaryProject.projectType: operational information architecture and document-generation framework
primaryProject.projectGoal: Capture operational events once as structured data, preserve source evidence, translate those events into management categories, and generate forms, schedules, reports, approvals, and later analysis without repeatedly re-entering the same facts.
primaryProject.projectPhase: conceptual lesson and first-script design guidance
primaryProject.contributionType: information-translation model, source-preservation rule, structured-record design, automatic document-generation workflow, observability framework, and inventory expansion
primaryProject.identificationBasis: The lesson explicitly describes housekeeping as an information system and defines a translation boundary between operational events, structured records, management classifications, and official paperwork.

relatedProjects.relationshipDescription: The lesson proposes generating official forms and printable PDFs from structured records rather than recreating the information manually each time.
relatedProjects.impact: Required paperwork can remain familiar, portable, signable, and accepted while the underlying information becomes reusable and machine-readable.
relatedProjects.identificationBasis: The document explicitly defines JSON-to-sheet-to-PDF workflows and lists the first script's responsibilities.

relatedProjects.relationshipType: derived outputs from shared operational events
relatedProjects.relationshipDescription: One overtime or staffing event can generate roster updates and calendar events from the same structured record.
relatedProjects.impact: Availability, coverage, dates, times, and reasons can remain synchronized across operational views.
relatedProjects.identificationBasis: The lesson explicitly lists roster updates and calendar events among outputs generated from one record.

relatedProjects.relationshipDescription: The lesson expands inventory beyond materials and equipment to include tools, templates, records, and data structures.
relatedProjects.impact: Scripts, forms, schemas, records, and mappings become visible resources that can be tracked and reused.
relatedProjects.identificationBasis: The document explicitly defines six inventory classes.

relatedProjects.relationshipDescription: Source images, structured records, generated outputs, and approval states remain linked so later review and analysis can distinguish original evidence from interpretation and presentation.
relatedProjects.impact: The system supports traceability, historical reconstruction, and reuse of the same facts across many representations.
relatedProjects.identificationBasis: The source explicitly requires the original image to remain linked to the structured transcription.

sharedFoundations.name: Source evidence
sharedFoundations.relationshipDescription: Original paper, photographed forms, and direct operational events remain available as the evidentiary source.
sharedFoundations.impact: Structured interpretation and generated documents can be checked against the original evidence.

sharedFoundations.name: Structured operational record
sharedFoundations.relationshipDescription: Operational facts are stored in a machine-readable form such as JSON and may also be represented in a Google Sheet.
sharedFoundations.impact: The same event can drive many outputs without repeated manual entry.

sharedFoundations.name: Translation rules
sharedFoundations.relationshipDescription: Operational language is mapped to pay codes, approval fields, accounting periods, compliance categories, signatures, and official layouts.
sharedFoundations.impact: Management paperwork can be generated from operational facts while preserving both perspectives.

projectContext.relationshipSummary: The lesson defines a layered architecture in which source evidence is preserved, structured records become reusable, translation rules map operations into administrative language, and many official or analytical outputs are generated from one event.

subject.mainFocus: Explaining how operational events can be captured once, preserved as structured records, translated into management categories, and reused to generate forms, schedules, reports, approvals, dashboards, and analysis.
subject.description: A housekeeping information-systems lesson covering inputs, internal state, outputs, translation boundaries, JSON records, automatic document generation, source evidence, observability, broader inventory classes, and the first script to build.

audience: people designing automated forms and records
prerequisites: basic familiarity with forms, spreadsheets, and departmental paperwork
learningContext.learningPurpose: Teach how housekeeping operations can be represented as an information system and how structured data can bridge operational language, administrative requirements, printed forms, and later analysis.
learningContext.instructionalApproach: Uses tables, flow diagrams, a concrete overtime JSON example, contrasting source and output roles, a practical workflow, a design rule, and review questions.

learningObjectives.description: Explain housekeeping as an information system with inputs, internal state, and outputs.
Distinguish supervisor language from management language and identify the structured record as the translation boundary.
Explain why the structured record should be created before the official paper or PDF representation.
Describe both the preferred digital-first workflow and the historical-paper transcription workflow.
Explain why original images or source documents should remain linked to structured transcriptions.
Identify multiple outputs that can be generated from one operational event.
Define observability across staffing, work, administrative, and resource states.
Recognize tools, templates, records, and data structures as inventory alongside materials and equipment.
Describe the responsibilities of the first script that maps structured data into a generated form.

principles.title: Digitization is not the final goal
principles.statement: The goal is to build a reliable information system, not merely to reproduce paperwork electronically.
principles.explanation: Operational events should be recorded once, translated into the language required by management, and reused for many outputs.
principles.importance: This prevents digital tools from becoming faster versions of repetitive clerical work.

principles.title: Housekeeping has inputs, internal state, and outputs
principles.statement: Physical work is governed by information entering the department, changing inside it, and leaving as completed conditions or records.
principles.explanation: Staffing requests, work orders, assignments, pending work, completed units, forms, and reports are all part of one information system.
principles.importance: It makes the department observable as a system rather than only as visible physical labor.

principles.title: The structured record is the translation boundary
principles.statement: Operational events should first become structured records before being translated into management categories and official forms.
principles.explanation: The record preserves what happened while translation rules express it as pay codes, approvals, accounting periods, compliance categories, and signatures.
principles.importance: It allows operational truth and administrative representation to remain linked without being confused.

principles.title: Structured data should precede paperwork
principles.statement: Create the machine-readable record first and generate the paper or PDF representation from it.
principles.explanation: JSON preserves meaning, the PDF preserves appearance, and paper preserves portability and signatures.
principles.importance: Each representation can perform its proper role without becoming the sole source of information.

principles.title: Preserve source evidence
principles.statement: A structured transcription or interpretation should remain linked to the original paper or image.
principles.explanation: The JSON is not identical to the source evidence; it is a structured reading of that evidence.
principles.importance: Traceability supports correction, review, audit, and confidence.

principles.title: One event should support many outputs
principles.statement: The same operational event should not be entered independently into rosters, calendars, forms, approvals, totals, and analysis.
principles.explanation: One structured record can generate every required representation and calculation.
principles.importance: This reduces duplication, inconsistency, and clerical effort.

principles.title: Observability includes administrative and resource state
principles.statement: A supervisor needs visibility not only into work and staffing but also into forms, approvals, supplies, tools, scripts, and templates.
principles.explanation: The state of paperwork and information resources can constrain operations as directly as physical shortages.
principles.importance: It broadens supervision from task observation to system condition.

principles.title: Information resources belong in inventory
principles.statement: Tools, templates, records, schemas, mappings, and field definitions are departmental resources.
principles.explanation: They are required to perform and reproduce administrative and operational work.
principles.importance: This supports ownership, maintenance, reuse, and continuity of digital capabilities.

principles.title: Enter once, translate, and generate
principles.statement: Enter the facts once, preserve the source, translate the event into required categories, and generate every representation from the same record.
principles.explanation: The first script should load structured data, map fields, generate the output, name it consistently, link it to the source, and track approvals.
principles.importance: This is the lesson's governing design rule and implementation direction.

concepts.name: Housekeeping information system
concepts.definition: A model of the department as a system that receives information, maintains internal state, and produces physical and administrative outputs.
relationships: Outputs demonstrate what the department produced
examples: A staffing request changes assignments and produces a roster update
An inspection requirement produces completed work and an inspection report
misconceptions: Housekeeping is only physical work rather than physical work coordinated through information

concepts.name: Translation boundary
concepts.definition: The point where an operational event becomes structured data and is then mapped into administrative categories and official paperwork.
relationships: Separates operational language from management language
examples: Converting overtime dates and hours into pay codes, approval fields, and an official Kronos layout
misconceptions: The official form itself is the only meaningful representation of the event

concepts.name: Structured record
concepts.definition: A machine-readable representation of an event with explicit fields and values.
relationships: Can be stored in a sheet
Can generate PDFs and other outputs
Should remain linked to source evidence
examples: An overtime record containing employee, department, supervisor, week ending, time entries, and signature states
misconceptions: A formatted PDF and a structured record perform the same function

concepts.name: Source record
concepts.definition: The original evidence from which a structured transcription or interpretation is created.
relationships: May be a paper form or photographed image
Should remain linked to the structured record
misconceptions: The transcription makes the original evidence unnecessary

concepts.name: Representation
concepts.definition: A form in which the same underlying information is expressed for a particular purpose.
relationships: Roster preserves assignment and availability context
examples: One overtime event represented as JSON, a sheet row, a calendar event, and an official form

concepts.name: Observability
concepts.definition: The system's ability to expose current and recent staffing, work, administrative, and resource conditions.
examples: Seeing which forms are generated, signed, approved, submitted, or missing
misconceptions: Observability concerns only active physical tasks

concepts.name: Information-resource inventory
concepts.definition: An inventory that includes digital tools, templates, records, and data structures in addition to materials and equipment.
examples: Apps Script, QR codes, Kronos templates, completed forms, JSON schemas, and field mappings
misconceptions: Inventory consists only of consumable physical supplies

concepts.name: Approval state
concepts.definition: A structured status indicating whether required employee, supervisor, timekeeper, or management actions have occurred.
relationships: Can be stored as true or false
examples: Employee signed: true; supervisor signed: false
misconceptions: Approval status must exist only as an unreadable handwritten mark on paper

examples.title: Overtime event as a structured record
examples.scenario: An employee works extra hours that must later be represented in an official administrative form.
walkthrough: Record employee name, ID, department, supervisor, and week ending.
Store date, begin time, end time, pay type, and total hours.
Track employee, supervisor, and timekeeper signature states.
Map the structured values into the required form fields.
examples.result: The event can be preserved as JSON, stored in a sheet, and used to generate a printable form.
examples.lesson: Meaning should be stored independently from the visual document used to submit it.

examples.title: Converting a historical handwritten form
examples.scenario: An older paper record must be added to the structured information system.
walkthrough: Review and correct the extracted values.
Save the result as structured JSON.
Link the JSON back to the original image.
examples.result: Historical evidence becomes searchable and reusable without discarding the original source.
examples.lesson: Transcription improves usability, while the image preserves evidence.

examples.title: One overtime event, many outputs
examples.scenario: One overtime event affects staffing, scheduling, administrative approval, totals, and historical planning.
walkthrough: Place the record in an approval queue.
Retain the event for historical analysis.
examples.result: Multiple synchronized outputs are produced without re-entering the same event independently.
examples.lesson: One canonical record reduces duplication and inconsistency.

procedures.title: Generate required paperwork from a structured record
procedures.purpose: Create official printable documents while preserving reusable machine-readable data.

steps.expectedResult: The event is captured without duplicative form entry.

steps.instruction: Store the facts in a structured record.
steps.expectedResult: The record can be validated, queried, and reused.

steps.instruction: Apply translation rules to map the record into official fields.
steps.expectedResult: Operational language is converted into the required management representation.

steps.instruction: Generate the printable form or PDF.
steps.expectedResult: The accepted visual layout is produced.

steps.instruction: Print, sign, and submit when paper or signatures are required.
steps.expectedResult: The official process remains compatible with organizational requirements.

steps.instruction: Link the generated document and approval states to the source record.

verification: Generated fields match the structured source values.
The output has a consistent filename.
Required signature and approval states are visible.
The generated document links back to the original record.

procedures.title: Convert historical paper into structured data
procedures.purpose: Add older records to the information system while preserving original evidence.

steps.instruction: Photograph or scan the original paper.
steps.expectedResult: A durable image of the source exists.
The paper content becomes a draft structured record.

steps.instruction: Review and correct the extracted values.
steps.expectedResult: Errors or ambiguities are resolved before storage.
The historical event becomes searchable and reusable.

steps.instruction: Link the record to the original image.
steps.expectedResult: The interpretation remains traceable to evidence.

verification: The structured record contains the required fields.
The record identifies its source image.
Corrections are distinguishable from the original evidence.

procedures.title: Build the first information-translation script
procedures.purpose: Create the smallest useful automation that converts structured data into a linked official output.

steps.expectedResult: The script has one validated source object.

steps.instruction: Map the values to the correct form fields.
steps.expectedResult: Each required administrative field has a defined source.

steps.instruction: Generate a printable document or PDF.
steps.expectedResult: The official layout is produced automatically.

steps.instruction: Save the output using a consistent name.
steps.expectedResult: The file can be identified and retrieved reliably.

steps.instruction: Link the generated document to the original record.
steps.expectedResult: The output and source remain connected.

steps.instruction: Track signature and approval status as explicit values.

verification: The output reproduces the mapped values correctly.
The filename follows the selected convention.
The source and output links resolve.
Approval states survive reload and can be queried.

warnings.title: Do not merely digitize paperwork
warnings.risk: The department may reproduce the same repeated entry and disconnected records in electronic form.
warnings.avoid: Treating the PDF or online form as the architecture rather than as one representation.
warnings.correctiveAction: Create a reusable structured record and generate required representations from it.

warnings.title: Do not recreate the same information for every form
warnings.risk: Independent entry causes duplication, inconsistency, missing updates, and unnecessary clerical work.
warnings.avoid: Entering one event separately into a roster, calendar, form, approval queue, and report.
warnings.correctiveAction: Use one canonical event record to generate all outputs.

warnings.title: Do not discard the original source after transcription
warnings.risk: Errors or interpretations in the structured record may become impossible to verify.
warnings.avoid: Treating extracted JSON as identical to the original paper or image.
warnings.correctiveAction: Keep the original source linked to the structured record.

warnings.title: Do not use the official paper as the only data store
warnings.risk: The information remains difficult to reuse for totals, dashboards, schedules, approvals, or analysis.
warnings.avoid: Storing meaning only in the visual layout.
warnings.correctiveAction: Store explicit fields in a structured record and treat the paper as a generated representation.

warnings.title: Do not limit inventory to physical supplies
warnings.risk: Critical scripts, forms, schemas, records, and mappings may remain unowned, undocumented, or unavailable.
warnings.avoid: Ignoring information resources because they are not consumable materials.
warnings.correctiveAction: Track tools, templates, records, and data structures as inventory classes.

reviewQuestions.question: Why is a paper form useful even when the underlying data is digital?
reviewQuestions.answerSummary: It remains familiar, portable, signable, and accepted by the organization, while the structured record preserves reusable meaning.

reviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between a source record and a structured record?
reviewQuestions.answerSummary: The source record is the original evidence; the structured record is a machine-readable transcription or representation derived from it.

reviewQuestions.question: Why should both the operational event and the management classification be preserved?
reviewQuestions.answerSummary: The operational event records what actually happened, while the classification expresses it in the administrative language required for approvals, accounting, compliance, and forms.

reviewQuestions.question: How does observability improve supervisory control?
reviewQuestions.answerSummary: It exposes staffing, work, administrative, and resource states so the supervisor does not have to reconstruct the department from memory.

reviewQuestions.question: What outputs can be generated from one overtime record?
reviewQuestions.answerSummary: Roster updates, calendar events, official adjustment forms, approval-queue entries, weekly totals, and historical analysis.

reviewQuestions.question: Why does the lesson say JSON, PDF, and paper have different purposes?
reviewQuestions.answerSummary: JSON preserves explicit meaning, PDF preserves visual appearance, and paper provides portability and signatures.

reviewQuestions.question: What should the first information-translation script do?
reviewQuestions.answerSummary: Load structured data, map it to form fields, generate and name a printable output, link it to the source, and track signatures and approvals.

general.summary: Housekeeping Information Translation explains how operational events can be preserved once as structured data and reused to produce official paperwork, schedules, records, approvals, dashboards, and analysis.
keyPoints: Housekeeping is an information system as well as a physical-work system.
Operational and management language should be connected through structured records.
Structured data should come before generated paperwork.
Original source evidence should remain linked.
One event can generate many outputs.
Observability includes work, staffing, administrative, and resource state.
Digital tools and schemas are inventory resources.
The first script should map one structured record into one linked official output.

technical.summary: The lesson presents a conceptual architecture using Google Forms or an app for capture, JSON as the semantic record, Google Sheets for tabular storage, Apps Script or equivalent logic for mapping, and generated PDF or paper for official representation.
keyPoints: The source includes a sample overtime JSON object.
Historical paper intake follows image, extraction, review, correction, JSON, and source-linking stages.
The first script requires deterministic field mapping and consistent output naming.
The lesson does not provide a deployed script, API, form template, or final schema.

projectSpecificLessons: Klinswork can use one operational record to drive both employee-facing and management-facing representations.
The current roster, calendar, inventory, and documentation tools can become outputs or consumers of shared event records.
Source images and generated documents should be linked through record identity rather than stored as unrelated files.
Approval state should be structured and queryable instead of visible only on paper.
generalLessons: A form is a transport representation, not necessarily the canonical record.
Meaning, appearance, portability, and signature each require different representations.
Translation rules should be explicit rather than embedded in repeated human clerical work.
One canonical event record reduces inconsistency across outputs.
Historical transcription should preserve source evidence.
Observability includes information resources and administrative state.
Templates, schemas, scripts, and records are operational assets.

recurringProblems.problem: The same event is re-entered into several systems.
recurringProblems.pattern: Rosters, calendars, official forms, approval queues, totals, and reports each receive independent versions of the same facts.

recurringProblems.problem: Official paperwork is treated as the canonical data store.
recurringProblems.pattern: Important meaning remains locked in a visual document that is difficult to query or reuse.

recurringProblems.problem: Structured transcriptions become detached from source evidence.
recurringProblems.pattern: Extracted fields are stored without a durable link to the original image or form.

recurringProblems.problem: Information resources are omitted from inventory.
recurringProblems.pattern: Scripts, templates, schemas, mappings, and completed records remain invisible despite being required for operations.
